Method

Participants

This sample procedure and analysis plan for each of the four hypotheses was preregistered at https://osf.io/zj3a6. The participants were recruited from an introductory psychology course at the University of Turku, Finland. The participants obtained course credit for their participation. All of them were native speakers of Finnish with no reading disability or abnormal vision. In accordance with the preregistered protocol, a total of 50 participants was recruited.

[PAPER_0044, relevance_score=0.348] Procedure

The session took place in a small experimental room. The software used to control the experiment (stimulus presentation, recording of responses) was DMDX (Forster & Forster, 2003). The stimuli were presented with a monospaced font (Courier New). We used the typical arrangement in the masked priming procedure. Each trial began by presenting a mask composed of # signs in the center of the computer screen for 500 ms-this mask had the same length as the prime/target.

[PAPER_0038, relevance_score=0.238] Materials

We selected 170 target words of 5-6 letters long in Finnish, all nouns or adjectives, from a newspaper corpus accessed by WordMill (Laine & Virtanen, 1999). The target words contained 2-3 syllables and had an average frequency of 53 occurrences per million words (range = 1-1,146 per million). All of them contained at least one diacritical vowel (i.e., ä or ö; e.g., MÄNTY, PÖYTÄ). For each target word, we created five prime conditions.

While not preregistered, we also report the Bayes Factors for each comparison-these values were obtained with the BayesFactor package (Morey et al., 2015) in R using the default priors.

[PAPER_0065, relevance_score=0.223] One could argue that vowel harmony effects could be more salient for PÖYTÄ-type words (i.e., with a noticeable disharmony for primes like poytä given the diacritics in ä) than for MÄNTY-type words (for which a prime like manty might be less salient). Post hoc analyses of the two masked priming experiments showed that the pattern of priming effects was very similar for the two types of items-note that 133 of 170 words were PÖYTÄ-type of words.

items.paper_content_quotes:
[PAPER_0047, relevance_score=0.313] Results and Discussion

In accordance with the preregistered protocol, RTs shorter than 250 ms or greater than 3 SDs from the overall participants' mean were excluded from the latency analyses. The averages per condition for RTs and error rates are shown in Table 1.

(Generalized) linear mixed effects models were used to analyze the data using the lme4 package (Bates et al., 2015) in the R environment (R Development Core Team, 2020). Participants' and items' intercepts and slopes were entered as the random effects.
items.paper_content_summary: The paper reports excluding RTs below 250 ms or beyond 3 SDs from the mean and imposing a 2-second response deadline. An exploratory analysis used 48 participants because two Author Recognition Test scores were misplaced. [PAPER_0047] [PAPER_0045] [FULLPAPER_0133]

items.registration_content_summary: The registration specifies excluding RTs below 250 ms or beyond 3 SDs from the overall mean. Responses exceeding the 2-second deadline would automatically be classified as errors by DMDX. [PREREG_0017]
